These CORE requirements have no task covering them yet (a task covers a requirement by listing its id in requirement_ids):
- R-017: NaturalLanguage-based mood/sentiment score is generated per transcript and presented as a hedged rough polarity signal, never clinical framing
- R-018: Tag and mood suggestions are editable and dismissible; never silently applied as fact
- R-022: Entries support @-mention autocomplete to link to another entry
- R-023: Mentions/backlinks resolve via the target entry's persistent UUID, never by matching display-title text
- R-024: Renaming an entry never breaks or misdirects any existing mention of it
- R-025: Backlinks ('linked from') are computed live from the local store on every view, never stored as a separately maintained table
- R-026: Deleting an entry leaves zero dangling or duplicate backlinks in any live backlink query
- R-027: A forward @-mention pointing at a since-deleted entry renders as a visually distinct 'broken link' indicator rather than silently becoming plain text
- R-028: Duplicate @-mentions of the same target entry within one transcript collapse to a single backlink entry
- R-029: Self-mentions are disallowed at autocomplete time
- R-030: Demo entries and real entries are mutually unlinkable via @-mention autocomplete filtering by demo/real status
- R-031: Full-text search spans transcripts, tags, and mood
- R-032: Search results are ranked by a documented, deterministic relevance formula, not substring match order
- R-033: The relevance formula produces the documented ordering on a fixed two-entry test case
- R-034: Entries without a transcript yet remain findable via tags/mood/sketch metadata (documented expected behavior, not a defect)

Re-emit a SINGLE corrected ```tasks-json``` fenced block — the whole backlog, not a diff — that adds or updates tasks (via requirement_ids) so every one of these is covered by at least one task.

The build workers are assigned their lane's tasks from this block, so make it complete.
response:
One thing up front: I don't have the prior backlog or `requirements.json` available in this session (empty working directory, no prior turns with that data), so I can't produce a true diff against the existing backlog. What follows is a full reconstruction of a coherent backlog for this app (journal/notebook with transcripts, tags, mood, sketches, @-mention backlinks, and search), with dedicated, explicit tasks for all 15 gap requirements (R-017/018, R-022–R-034) plus inferred supporting tasks for the surrounding requirement range so the graph is self-consistent. If you have the actual existing backlog on hand, diff this against it — I flagged the reconstructed (non-given) requirement IDs so you can spot-check them against your real requirements.json.

Key design decisions baked into the tasks below:
- Mentions/backlinks resolve strictly by target UUID (R-023), never by title match, which is also what makes rename-safety (R-024) and dedup (R-028) tractable.
- Backlinks are computed live at view time from mention references stored on the source entry — no separate backlink table (R-025), so deletion cleanup (R-026) is "query correctness" rather than "table maintenance."
- Mood/tag suggestions are modeled as a distinct, editable/dismissible UI layer (R-018) sitting on top of an NLP scoring service that's explicitly hedged, non-clinical (R-017).
- Search (R-031–034) depends on the tag/mood/entry stores already existing, with the relevance formula and its fixed 2-entry test case as separate tasks so the formula is independently reviewable/testable.
